problem: Image-retrieval localization on topological maps (e.g. SPTM's SiameseNet) uses a single query image, so it picks wrong nodes when the map holds many similar-looking images (repetitive indoor scenes), causing navigation failures. Ground-truth poses for real images are also hard to obtain, which blocks supervised training on real data.
motivation: Accurate node localization is the key to topological image-based navigation with a monocular camera. Adjacent nodes share appearance and objects (spatial consistency), and the robot's recent motion history rules out look-alike but wrong nodes (temporal consistency). Simulator images provide GT poses, and real images can be added via semi-supervised learning to close the sim2real gap.
key_idea: Localize on a topological map with a graph convolutional LSTM (GIN-based) over per-node ResNet-18 similarity features, jointly using map-graph structure and time-series observations, trained with mixed simulator (GT pose) and real (nearest-node label) data.
insight: Ablations show that removing GCLSTM causes the largest drop (Not deviated AC 0.851 to 0.779; real-image map error 7.038 to 20.218), so the spatio-temporal aggregation is the main source of gain. The skip path helps (w/o skip AC 0.823), and mixing real images matters for real-data performance (w/o real image ME 16.728 vs 7.038), while sim-only is slightly better on the 1.0-2.0 deviated ME/AC* metric. Plugging the non-recurrent variant (SPTM+) into navigation gives no gain over SPTM with DVMPC, so the benefit comes from the GCLSTM.
method: Feature extraction module: ResNet-18 (ImageNet-pretrained, fine-tuned) encodes the current image and every node image; FC layers extract a similarity feature between the current image and each node; node features can be precomputed offline.

Spatio-temporal aggregation: GCLSTM (LSTM whose gate transforms are GIN graph convolutions over map edges) aggregates neighbouring-node and past-step features; a shared-weight FC skip path preserves self-node features.

Identification module: two FC layers give a scalar likelihood per node, and softmax over nodes gives the localization probability; the argmax node is the position. Trained with cross-entropy over tau=90 steps.

Semi-supervised sim2real training: simulator (iGibson, Matterport-scanned rooms) data with GT-pose-derived node labels, plus real Go Stanford data where G and O' come from the same sequence and the label is the nearest node; mini-batches randomly mix both.
Map sampler: builds a partial map G' of n'=200 nodes that always contains the GT nodes and is grown by randomly adding connected neighbours; it also acts as graph augmentation.
Navigation system: localization (ours), planning (Dijkstra subgoal images), control (DVMPC velocity from subgoal and current image), run at 3 fps.

setting.backbone: ResNet-18 + GCLSTM (GIN) + FC (trained; ResNet ImageNet-pretrained); DVMPC controller
setting.training_data: iGibson simulator images from 36 rooms (108 trajectories, scanned with Matterport 2) plus real images from the Go Stanford dataset (106,560 real images of 12 buildings, no GT pose)
setting.observation: monocular 360° RGB image (Ricoh Theta S on the real robot) plus a topological map of node images
setting.action_space: continuous linear/angular velocity from DVMPC toward subgoal images; localization outputs a node index
setting.privileged: none at test time (topological map built from prior teleoperated trajectories)

numbers_note: No canonical benchmark from the list; results are on the authors' own iGibson/GS localization and navigation setup. Localization test (unseen sim rooms, Table 1): ours AC/AC* 0.851/0.981 Not deviated, 0.798/0.950 Deviated<=1.0, 0.383/0.604 for 1.0<Deviated<=2.0, 0.775/0.894 on real images (ME 7.038). Navigation sim mean (Table 2, 3 areas, 100 trials each): SR 0.88, CR 0.06, TR 0.06, CovR 91.44. Real robot mean (Table 3, 3 envs, 10 trials each): SR 0.73, CovR 89.66.
results: The method beats Pixel MSE, SSIM, SiameseNet and NetVLAD on nearly all localization metrics in unseen environments (e.g. Not-deviated AC 0.851 vs 0.788 for NetVLAD; real-image map error 7.038 vs 12.603). In simulated navigation the mean SR is 0.88 vs 0.83 for SPTM with DVMPC, and on the real robot 0.73 vs 0.60.
limitations: Localization degrades when the robot deviates strongly from the mapped trajectory (AC only 0.383 for deviation 1.0-2.0); the authors list this as future work.
Real-image evaluation has no loop closure or deviation and no GT poses, so map error is large for all methods; the real-robot study is small (10 trials x 3 environments).
The map must be built beforehand from teleoperated trajectories, and inference cost grows with node count since all nodes are processed.
